candidates.exact_span: Animals shall not be allowed to graze on the land for 30 days after application of sewage sludge.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a time-bound land-use restriction tied to sludge application; whether grazing occurred within 30 days after application affects whether this permit obligation was applicable and satisfied for FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: Turf grown on land where sewage sludge is applied shall not be harvested for 1 year after application of the sewage sludge when the harvested turf is placed on either land with a high potential for public exposure or a lawn, unless otherwise specified by the permitting authority.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Applicability depends on turf use destination, land exposure classification, and possible permitting-authority exceptions; different readings of those conditions change which monitoring/obligations apply (B) and whether missing harvest evidence reflects a documented no-requirement state versus unresolved applicability (C).

candidates.exact_span: Public access to land with a high potential for public exposure shall be restricted for 1 year after application of sewage sludge.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether land qualifies as high potential for public exposure determines if the 1-year access restriction is operative; classification changes evaluated obligations (B) and how to classify periods without access-restriction evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: Public access to land with a low potential for public exposure shall be restricted for 30 days after application of sewage sludge.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Low-exposure classification triggers a different restriction period than high-exposure land; interpretation of site classification changes which obligation applies (B) and the evidentiary state for missing access records (C).

candidates.exact_span: All bulk sewage sludge that is applied to agricultural land, forest, a public contact site, or a reclamation site shall be treated by one of the following alternatives 1 through 10 for Vector Attraction Reduction.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Vector-attraction treatment is required only for bulk sludge applied to enumerated site types; whether a given application meets those site-type conditions changes which compliance pathway and numeric criteria must be evaluated (A) and which monitoring obligations are in scope (B).

candidates.exact_span: If bulk sewage sludge is applied to a home garden, or bagged sewage sludge is applied to the land, only alternative 1 through alternative 8 shall be used.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Home-garden and bagged-application classifications limit allowable vector-attraction alternatives to 1–8 rather than 1–10; different readings of application type change which numeric limits and demonstration methods are eligible for compliance comparison (A) and which requirements are applicable (B).

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 1 - The mass of volatile solids in the sewage sludge shall be reduced by a minimum of 38%.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets an enforceable 38% volatile-solids-reduction threshold; if volatile-solids measurements are reported, a different interpretation of reduction calculation or baseline could change exceedance determination (A) and whether this alternative's monitoring pathway was required (B).

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 2 - If Alternative 1 cannot be met for an anaerobically digested sludge, demonstration can be made by digesting a portion of the previously digested sludge anaerobically in the laboratory in a bench-scale unit for 40 additional days at a temperature between 30 and 37 degrees Celsius. Volatile solids must be reduced by less than 17% to demonstrate compliance.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Provides a conditional bench-scale demonstration pathway with numeric thresholds (40 days, 30–37 °C, <17% VS reduction); whether Alternative 1 failure is established and whether bench-scale results meet these criteria changes limit comparison (A), which monitoring method applies (B), and whether absent bench-scale data is a documented alternative pathway or unresolved evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 3 - If Alternative 1 cannot be met for an aerobically digested sludge, demonstration can be made by digesting a portion of the previously digested sludge with a percent solid of 2% or less aerobically in the laboratory in a bench-scale unit for 30 additional days at 20 degrees Celsius. Volatile solids must be reduced by less than 15% to demonstrate compliance.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Conditional aerobic bench-scale pathway with percent-solids, duration, temperature, and <15% VS-reduction criteria; interpretation of digested-sludge type, solids concentration, and demonstration results changes applicable numeric limits (A), required monitoring (B), and classification of missing demonstration data (C).

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 4 - The specific oxygen uptake rate (SOUR) for sewage sludge treated in an aerobic process shall be equal to or less than 1.5 milligrams of oxygen per hour per gram of total solids (dry weight basis) at a temperature of 20 degrees Celsius.
candidates.computation_change_reason: States an enforceable SOUR numeric limit at a specified temperature and dry-weight basis; different interpretation of measurement conditions or reported SOUR values could change exceedance findings (A) and whether SOUR monitoring was the operative compliance method (B).

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 5 - Sewage sludge shall be treated in an aerobic process for 14 days or longer. During that time, the temperature of the sewage sludge shall be higher than 40 degrees Celsius and the average temperature of the sewage sludge shall be higher than 45 degrees Celsius.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Imposes duration and temperature numeric criteria for aerobic treatment; interpretation of treatment duration and instantaneous versus average temperature records affects limit exceedance evaluation (A) and whether temperature/duration monitoring was required for this pathway (B).

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 6 - The pH of sewage sludge shall be raised to 12 or higher by alkali addition and, without the addition of more alkali shall remain at 12 or higher for two hours and then at 11.5 or higher for an additional 22 hours at the time the sewage sludge is used or disposed; at the time the sewage sludge is prepared for sale or given away in a bag or other container.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines time-staged pH numeric limits and ties measurement timing to use/disposal or bagging events; different readings of when the clock starts and whether pH was maintained without further alkali change applicable limits (A), monitoring timing obligations (B), and how to treat missing pH time-series evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 7 - The percent solids of sewage sludge that does not contain unstabilized solids generated in a primary wastewater treatment process shall be equal to or greater than 75 % based on the moisture content and total solids prior to mixing with other materials.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Applies a 75% solids threshold only when unstabilized primary solids are absent and requires measurement before mixing; interpretation of solids content, mixing timing, and unstabilized-solids presence changes numeric limit applicability (A), monitoring requirements (B), and whether missing solids data reflects non-applicability or unresolved evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: Unstabilized solids are defined as organic materials in sewage sludge that have not been treated in either an aerobic or anaerobic treatment process.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines unstabilized solids, which gates Alternative 7 applicability; different interpretation of prior treatment history changes whether the 75% solids limit applies (A), which monitoring pathway is required (B), and how to classify cases lacking treatment-process evidence (C).
